title.raw: Quashing of FIR: Meaning, Grounds, Documents, Procedure and Fees (Bombay High Court)
title.rendered: Quashing of FIR: Meaning, Grounds, Documents, Procedure and Fees (Bombay High Court)

content.raw:
In short: Quashing means cancelling. When the High Court quashes an FIR or a criminal case, it sets it aside and the case ends without a trial. A quash petition is the application that asks the High Court to do this. In Maharashtra it is filed at the Bombay High Court in Mumbai under Section 528 BNSS (old Section 482 CrPC), often together with Article 226. The court allows it only on narrow grounds. This guide covers the meaning, grounds, documents, procedure and how fees work.

Quashing meaning: what it means to quash an FIR

To "quash" means to set aside or cancel. Quashing of an FIR means the High Court cancels the FIR, so the police investigation and any case based on it stop. A quash petition asks the High Court to cancel an FIR, the chargesheet, or the criminal case that has come out of it. If the court agrees, that case ends.

You will also see it called a "quashing petition", "FIR quashing petition" or "quashing in High Court". A quash petition is not a bail application and not an appeal. It is a separate, limited remedy, and the court uses it sparingly.

For the law, the stages and interim relief, see our page on FIR quashing at the Bombay High Court.

Grounds for quashing of FIR

The High Court does not quash an FIR just because the accused says it is false. The petition must fit a recognised ground. In plain words, the main grounds are:

  1. No offence is made out. Even if every allegation in the FIR is taken as true, no offence is disclosed.
  2. The allegations are absurd or impossible. No sensible person could find enough ground to proceed on them.
  3. A civil dispute has been given a criminal colour. Money, property or contract disputes sometimes become FIRs. The court asks whether the FIR actually discloses a crime or only a broken agreement.
  4. The case is malicious. It was filed to take revenge or settle a private score.
  5. The law bars the case. For example, a required sanction is missing, or a statute provides its own remedy.
  6. The parties have settled a private dispute. This applies mostly to matrimonial and commercial matters, and never to serious offences.

These come from the Supreme Court's decisions in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal (1992) and Gian Singh v. State of Punjab (2012). Both are explained on the service page. The court looks at the FIR and the documents, not at who is likely to win at trial.

FIRs that are commonly taken to the High Court

  • Matrimonial cases under Section 85 BNS (old Section 498A IPC), usually after a settlement. See 498A and domestic violence defence.
  • Cheating and breach-of-trust cases under Section 318(4) and Section 316(2) BNS (old Sections 420 and 406 IPC) that began as business or money disputes.
  • Complaints that look like a way to pressure someone over a payment or a property matter. See false FIR: legal remedies.

Whether any of these can be quashed depends on the facts. Being in one of these groups does not decide the outcome.

Documents required for quashing of FIR

The petition is decided on papers, so the file matters. The table shows what to collect and why.

DocumentWhy it matters
Copy of the FIRThe court first reads the allegations as written. Note the police station and crime number.
Chargesheet and annexures (if filed)Shows what the police collected and which offences they have charged.
Court orders so farBail orders, remand orders and any order taking cognisance show where the case stands.
Police notices, summons or warrantsShows whether you are being called in or are at risk of arrest.
Supporting documentsAgreements, bank statements, messages, emails and receipts that show the dispute is civil or the allegation is baseless.
Settlement or compromise deed (if any)Needed for settlement-based petitions. Both sides should sign it, with affidavits.
Petitioner's affidavit and ID proofVerifies the facts stated in the petition.

If you do not have the FIR, see how to check an FIR registered against you in Maharashtra.

Quash petition procedure at the Bombay High Court, step by step

The steps below are the usual sequence. Details can vary with the matter and the court's rules and rosters.

  1. Review the papers. The FIR, chargesheet and orders are read to see whether the case fits a ground. If a settlement is involved, its terms are checked.
  2. Choose the remedy. Quashing is not always the right step. Where arrest is the immediate risk, anticipatory bail may be needed. Where the trial court can decide the point, discharge may be better.
  3. Draft the petition. It is drafted under Section 528 BNSS and, where suitable, Article 226. It sets out the facts, the ground, and the orders sought. The Supreme Court has said that once a Magistrate has taken cognisance, Article 226 is not available and Section 528 is the route.
  4. File at the Bombay High Court in Mumbai. There is no Pune bench, so a petition about a Pune or Pimpri-Chinchwad FIR is filed in Mumbai. The registry checks the papers, and the matter is then listed for hearing.
  5. First hearing and notice. The State of Maharashtra, and usually the complainant, are given notice. Any request for interim relief is argued here.
  6. Replies and final hearing. The other side may file replies. Both sides then argue. In a settlement case the compromise deed is placed before the court.
  7. Order. The court can quash the FIR and proceedings in whole or in part, or dismiss the petition. If it dismisses the petition, the case continues before the trial court. An order of the High Court can be challenged in the Supreme Court.

Interim relief: what to expect

Many people expect the High Court to stop an arrest at the first hearing. That is not automatic. In Neeharika Infrastructure v. State of Maharashtra (2021), the Supreme Court said that orders staying an investigation or directing "no coercive steps" should not be passed routinely. It said that, normally, the accused should apply for anticipatory bail instead. Interim protection is possible in exceptional cases, with reasons.

Quash petition fees and costs

Advocate fees for a quash petition depend on the court and the stage of the case. They are agreed at consultation. There is no standard figure we can honestly give for every case. See criminal lawyer fees in Pune.

Other costs include court fees and the cost of certified copies and filing. The office can explain these at consultation.

In a 2026 order, a Bombay High Court judge held that costs can be imposed on the parties in a consent-quashing case. So the court itself may order costs.

Be careful of anyone who guarantees a result. No lawyer can promise that a petition will be allowed.

Frequently asked questions

What does quash petition mean?

It means a petition asking the High Court to cancel an FIR or a criminal case. "Quash" means to set aside. It is filed under Section 528 BNSS, which was Section 482 CrPC before 1 July 2024.

Can an FIR be quashed without the complainant's consent?

Yes, where the FIR discloses no offence or the case is clearly an abuse of process. The complainant's consent matters mainly in settlement-based quashing, where the court needs to see that the dispute is genuinely settled.

What happens to the trial if the FIR is quashed?

If the High Court quashes the FIR and the proceedings, the case based on that FIR ends. The court's order sets out exactly what is quashed, so the order itself should be read carefully. A partial quashing leaves the remaining part of the case alive.

Can I apply for bail while the quash petition is pending?

Yes. A quash petition does not replace bail. Many people seek anticipatory bail or regular bail separately. See bail after arrest for the basics.

Which documents are required for quashing of an FIR?

At a minimum, the FIR, the chargesheet if filed, all court orders, and the documents that support your case. For a settlement, add the signed compromise deed and affidavits. The table above lists each item and why it matters.

Do I need to go to Mumbai for a quash petition?

The petition is filed and heard at the Bombay High Court in Mumbai, because there is no Pune bench. Whether the petitioner must attend in person depends on the court's directions in the matter. The office is in Shivajinagar, Pune, and consultation can be by phone or video.

What is the difference between quashing and discharge?

Quashing is decided by the High Court and can be sought at any stage. Discharge is decided by the trial court, after the chargesheet, on the ground that there is not enough to frame a charge. See discharge application.

If you need advice on your situation, you can contact the office.

This page explains the law in general terms and is not legal advice. Every case depends on its own facts.

  • Latest judgments on quashing of FIR
